title: Chapter 111: Wangxian: Forgetting Envy 1
content:
Chapter 111

Now, the only one left walking beside him was Lan Wangji.

How lucky he was that the only person he actually wanted by his side happened to be Lan Wangji, too.

“Lan Zhan,” Wei Wuxian called softly.

“Mn.”

“You raised him well.”

Lan Wangji looked ahead. “You will see him often from now on.”

“I know.”

“Once Wen Ning sees Sizhui back to the Cloud Recesses, he can settle nearby. They can see each other whenever they wish.”

Wei Wuxian turned his head, watching his quiet profile. “Lan Zhan, were you scared I’d say ‘thank you’ just now?”

He smiled faintly, a bit self-deprecating. “It just hit me—in our past life, almost every single time our paths split, I’d throw a ‘thank you’ your way. And without fail, every time we ran into each other after that, I was in a worse state than before.”

Outside that courier station after slaughtering Wen Chao and Wen Zhuliu. In Yunmeng, tossing flowers from that wine pavilion. Standing on the Burial Mounds in Yiling, parting ways.

Every single time, he’d used those polite two words to draw a line in the sand between them, shoving Lan Wangji further away.

Lan Wangji walked in silence for a few beats before murmuring, “Between us, there is no need for ‘thank you’ or ‘sorry.’”

Wei Wuxian’s eyes lit up with a grin. “Fine by me. Let’s talk about other things, then. For instance…”

His voice dropped to a conspiratorial whisper, and he crooked a finger, beckoning Lan Wangji to lean in close. Thinking he had a secret to share, Lan Wangji stepped right up. Instead, Wei Wuxian caught him by the jaw, tipped his face upward, and leaned down to seal their lips together.

It was a long, slow, dizzying press of lips. When Wei Wuxian finally pulled back a fraction, their eyelashes fluttered against each other, his breath warm against Lan Wangji's cheek. "Well? How was that?"

Lan Wangji stared at him in stunned silence.

"Come on, Hanguang-jun, give me a little reaction here!"

Still, Lan Wangji offered nothing but wide, dazed eyes.

Wei Wuxian pouted playfully. "You're so cold! Aren't you supposed to tackle me into the dirt right about now and—"

Before the joke cleared his teeth, Lan Wangji’s arm whipped around the back of his neck, roughly dragging him down into another fierce, bruising kiss.

Little Apple nearly jumped out of its skin, its chewing jaws freezing in place like a carved wooden toy.

Seconds later, the poor beast was relieved of its rider entirely. Lan Wangji slid one arm around Wei Wuxian’s back, hooked the other under his knees, and swept him straight off the donkey’s saddle. They stumbled together into the thick brush off the path, tumbling into the grass. Lan Wangji pinned him to the ground, kissing him with a fierce, ravenous hunger that left Wei Wuxian seeing stars.

Panting against his lips, Wei Wuxian suddenly pushed at his chest. “Wait, hold on—hold up!”

Lan Wangji hovered over him, breathing heavily. “What is it?”

Wei Wuxian squinted, his eyes darting across their surroundings. “I’m getting serious déjà vu right now…”

A secluded forest, thick shrubs, wild grass. Demanding, unyielding hands. A kiss so desperate it bruised.

The pieces clicked together, and the urge to know was too loud to ignore. He tested the waters: “The Phoenix Mountain hunt… when I had that blindfold on. Lan Zhan, was that...”

He didn't even finish the sentence, and Lan Wangji didn't say a word, but his fingers twitched violently against Wei Wuxian’s shoulder.

Wei Wuxian propped himself up on an elbow and pressed his ear flat against Lan Wangji’s chest. Beneath the pale linen, his heart was hammering like a frantic war drum.

Wei Wuxian’s jaw dropped. “Holy shit. Itwasyou?”

Lan Wangji swallowed hard. “I…”

“Lan Zhan, you sly dog! Who knew you had it in you? You really pulled a stunt like that?”

Lan Wangji kept his mouth shut, ears blazing.

“Do you have any idea how many years I spent convinced some shy maiden had a massive crush on me and couldn't work up the nerve to confess?!”

More silence.

Wei Wuxian gasped, leaning in. “You were harboring dirty thoughts about me all the way back then?!”

Lan Wangji buried his face against Wei Wuxian's neck, his voice muffled and thick with shame. "I... knew it was wrong. Entirely improper."

Wei Wuxian remembered finding him later that day, furiously venting his rage by obliterating trees in the forest. "So that was why you were so pissed off?!"

All this time, he’d assumed Lan Wangji was angry at someone else. He had never dreamed the man was tearing himself apart with self-loathing—furious at his own lack of control, sickened by his momentary lapse in restraint, horrified that he had taken advantage of someone’s vulnerability in direct violation of every clan rule he had ever lived by.

Seeing Lan Wangji keeping his head tucked so low, practically retreating into self-flagellation, Wei Wuxian reached up and affectionately scratched beneath his chin.

“Hey, come on, don't look so miserable about it. Knowing you stole a kiss from me that early makes me thrilled! That was my first kiss, you know. Congratulations, Hanguang-jun.”

Lan Wangji’s eyes snapped up. “Your first?”

“Yeah, obviously! Who else?”

Lan Wangji stared at him intently, an unreadable undercurrent stirring behind the pale gold of his eyes. “Then…”

“Then what? Trailing off like that isn’t really your style, Lan Zhan.”

Lan Wangji hesitated, the words catching in his throat. “Then… why… back then, why did you…”

Wei Wuxian frowned in genuine confusion. “Why did I what?”

Lan Wangji’s lips parted slightly before he forced out, “…Why didn’t you resist?”

Wei Wuxian blinked, momentarily stunned.

Lan Wangji’s voice dropped, laced with a dull, simmering ache. “You had no idea who it was. Why didn’t you fight it? And why… why did you tell me, afterward…”

Tell him what?

Then it hit him—when he’d run into Lan Wangji right after, he’d bragged shamelessly, talking a big game about being a seasoned expert and teasing Lan Wangji that his own first kiss would probably rot with him.

A slow grin broke across Wei Wuxian’s face. “Wait. You weren't just beating yourself up… what actually set you off was thinking I’d kissed someone else before, wasn't it?”

Lan Wangji offered no defense, only a mortified silence.

Wei Wuxian threw his arms around his neck, laughing so hard he could barely breathe. "Lan Zhan, are you an idiot?! You actually believed the garbage coming out of my mouth?! Ahaha!"

He was laughing way too hard, way too loud, and pushing his luck entirely too far. Finally, having had quite enough, Lan Wangji caught him by the waist and pinned him straight into the grass.

The rain had barely stopped, leaving the thick grass damp with droplets that seeped into Lan Wangji’s pristine white robes. Not that it mattered—Wei Wuxian was already stripping them off him in a frantic hurry.

“Stay still,” Wei Wuxian whispered, his voice dropping into something sweet and low as he shifted to kneel between Lan Wangji's thighs.

The scent of crushed greenery clung to Wei Wuxian’s throat and lips, meeting the cool, clean sandalwood radiating from Lan Wangji’s feverish skin. Kneeling, Wei Wuxian leaned down, pressing his lips to his forehead and charting a slow, deliberate path downward.

Between the brows. The bridge of the nose. The cheekbone. The curve of his lips. The sharp line of his jaw.

Down to his throat, the notch of his collarbone, the steady beat against his ribs.

Every kiss was gentle, almost reverent.

When his lips reached the tight plane of Lan Wangji’s lower abdomen and kept drifting lower, loose strands of hair spilling over Wei Wuxian's shoulders brushed against bare skin. Paired with the hot, shallow puffs of breath hovering over dangerously sensitive territory, it proved too much for Lan Wangji to bear. His hands came up to haul him back by the shoulders.

Wei Wuxian caught his wrists, pinning them back. “Don't move. I told you, I’ve got this.”

He pulled off his red ribbon, shaking his hair loose before casually tying it back out of his face, and dipped his head. Realizing what was about to happen, Lan Wangji’s composure completely fractured.

“Don’t,” he rasped, panicked.

“I want to,” Wei Wuxian murmured against his skin, and took him into his mouth.

Taking excruciating care to keep his teeth clear, he gently drew the burning, rigid length past his lips, sinking down as far as he could manage until the blunt head grazed the back of his throat. A faint gag hitched in his chest. Lan Wangji caught the slight discomfort instantly, his hands immediately reaching down to push him away. "Stop. That is enough."

Wei Wuxian nudged his hands aside, stubbornly beginning a slow, deliberate rhythm of drawing back and swallowing down.

"You..." Lan Wangji groaned, completely robbed of speech.

Wei Wuxian had devoured enough illicit illustrated scrolls in his youth to fill an entire archive room in the Cloud Recesses. Being as wickedly clever as he was, he put every bit of theoretical knowledge to work, using his tongue and lips in tandem to lavish meticulous, agonizing care on the searing heat between his jaws. Having his length engulfed in such wet, velvet warmth, treated with such devoted fervor, pushed Lan Wangji to the absolute edge; merely holding himself back from pinning Wei Wuxian down and taking him by force was an exercise in pure torture.

Wei Wuxian felt the man's breathing grow ragged, the fingers tangled in his hair tightening with bruising force. He picked up the pace, his jaw and throat aching with the strain, until a sudden, scalding wave pulsed deep against the back of his throat.

The liquid heat was thick and intoxicatingly musky, hitting his throat with such force that Wei Wuxian couldn't help a sharp, violent cough. He pulled back, spitting the length free as he doubled over, hacking into his hand.

Lan Wangji was beside himself, patting his back in uncharacteristic, panicked clumsiness. “Spit it out! Quick, spit it out!”

Wei Wuxian clamped a hand over his mouth, shaking his head. After a moment, he dropped his hand, sticking his tongue out with a cheeky, smug grin. “Swallowed it.”

His tongue was bright red, his lips swollen and flushed, and a stray streak of white clung to the corner of a wickedly pleased grin.

Lan Wangji stared at him, utterly struck dumb.

The most untouchable, ascetic cultivator in the realm had his icy reserve shattered beyond recognition. A soft peach flush dusted the corners of his eyes, leaving him looking thoroughly thoroughly loved—or thoroughly thoroughly ruined.

Wei Wuxian’s heart practically melted at the sight. Throwing a bare arm around his neck, he leaned in, pecking the corner of Lan Wangji’s lips, then his eyelid. “There, there. Don’t look so traumatized. You can do me next time, and you better do just as good a job, deal?”

His own mouth was still marked with Lan Wangji’s mess, and kissing him like that smeared a faint streak onto Lan Wangji’s lips too. Paired with his dazed, unblinking expression, he looked ridiculously endearing.

Wei Wuxian couldn't resist planting another loud kiss on his cheek. “Lan Zhan, I swear I'm so in love with you.”

Lan Wangji’s eyes slowly tracked over to him.

Maybe it was just the lighting, but Wei Wuxian thought he saw a dangerous storm brewing behind those pale irises.

Oblivious to the sheer, white-knuckled restraint threatening to snap right in front of him—and assuming Lan Wangji simply hadn't had his fill yet—Wei Wuxian grabbed the length that seemed to be filling up again, giving it a few slow strokes. “Gods, I could do this with you all day long.”

In a flash, Lan Wangji flipped them over, pinning him flat into the grass.

Their positions reversed in an instant. Feeling Lan Wangji start nipping hungrily at his neck and chest, Wei Wuxian chuckled, trying to nudge his head away. “No need to rush! I said next time we can—”

A sharp pang down below cut him off. Wei Wuxian winced, his brows knitting together. “Lan Zhan? What did you just put in there?”

He could tell it was a long, slender finger; the question was mostly pure reflex. He instinctively clamped his thighs together, but the intrusion only deepened as a second finger slid in right behind it.

For all the dirty books Wei Wuxian had flipped through, he’d never paid much attention to cutsleeve literature. He’d never thought he swung that way in the past, so he’d never bothered to satisfy his curiosity. In his mind, intimacy between two men was simple enough—kissing, holding each other, maybe a hand or a mouth here and there. He’d never thought past that. Now, pinned beneath Lan Wangji, feeling those fingers carefully working him open, it slowly dawned on him that this game was played entirely differently. Along with the faint, stretching ache came a spike of bewildered amusement.

When a third finger pushed inside, the humor vanished completely.

The fullness was already verging on uncomfortable, and three fingers weren't even close to the size of the thing he’d just had down his throat.

Panic started to set in. “Lan Zhan… Lan Zhan, hey, chill out for a second! Is this how it works?You sure you didn't get the anatomy wrong? Inthere? I really don't think that's—"

Lan Wangji was way past listening. He leaned down, silencing him with a rough, bruising kiss, dropped his hips, and pushed the head straight inside.

Wei Wuxian’s eyes blew wide as his knees jerked upward.

Pressed flush against each other, both their chests were heaving, their hearts racing out of control.

Lan Wangji’s voice was dark and hoarse: “…Sorry… I can’t hold back anymore.”

Seeing the man’s bloodshot eyes and the sheer strain on his face, Wei Wuxian knew damn well he’d brought this on himself. Gritting his teeth, he groaned, “If you can't hold back, then don't… But what the hell am I supposed to do right now?!”

Desperate times called for desperate measures; he was actually asking the guy pinning him down for advice.

Lan Wangji breathed, “…Relax.”

“Right, relax… just relax…” Wei Wuxian chanted under his breath.

The moment he loosened up just a fraction, Lan Wangji tested the waters, inching further in. Wei Wuxian’s stomach and hips snapped drum-tight on pure instinct.

Lan Wangji hesitated, his brow furrowing. “…Does it hurt?”

Clinging to his shoulders, Wei Wuxian’s body trembled uncontrollably, tears stinging the corners of his eyes. “Of course it hurts! It’s my first time, you idiot!”

The second the words left his mouth, he felt the hard length inside him swell even harder.

Having one's delicate insides forcefully invaded and stretched by something that didn't belong there wasn't a pleasant sensation by any stretch of the imagination. Yet realizing that a single whimper from him made Lan Wangji lose his composure like that, Wei Wuxian let out a helpless snort of laughter.

Being a man himself, he knew how miserable Lan Wangji had to feel, stalled halfway in. Yet even in this state, the man was holding back, refusing to force his way through.

A wave of tender warmth washed over Wei Wuxian’s chest. He looped his arms around Lan Wangji’s neck, pulling him down until his lips brushed against his ear. “Lan Zhan… dear Lan Zhan, Er-gege… I'll tell you the secret to it... Just kiss me. If you kiss me, it won't hurt…”

The pristine shell of Lan Wangji’s ear flared a brilliant crimson.

“...Stop,” he choked out, his voice shaking. “Don't call me that.”

Hearing the uncharacteristic stammer, Wei Wuxian let out a breathless laugh. “Don't like it? Fine, I’ll call you something else! Dear little Wangji? Zhan-er? Hanguang? Which one do you—ah, fuck, mmmph!”

Lan Wangji clamped his teeth down onto his lips and buried himself all the way to the hilt in one single, unyielding thrust.

Every scream was choked off right in Wei Wuxian’s throat. His hands locked onto Lan Wangji's shoulders, his brow tight with pain, tears spilling freely down his temples as his legs locked rigidly around the man's waist, terrified to move a muscle.

The harsh reality seemed to snap Lan Wangji back to his senses. Panting heavily, he whispered, “I’m sorry.”

Wei Wuxian shook his head, managing a strained, shaky smile. “You said it yourself… between us, you never have to say that.”

Lan Wangji leaned down, kissing him with clumsy, desperate gentleness. Wei Wuxian parted his lips, letting him deep inside, their tongues tangling until the worst of the ache dulled into a warm thrum. Through the haze, his gaze caught on the brutal brand scarred into Lan Wangji’s skin, right below the collarbone.

He reached up, his palm coming to rest flat over the ruined flesh, the playful grin slipping from his face. “Lan Zhan… tell me the truth. Did this have something to do with me, too?”

Silence fell for a long beat.

Finally, Lan Wangji murmured, “It was nothing. I had too much to drink.”

Back then, after escorting a hollow, half-mad Wei Wuxian back to the Burial Mounds following the bloodbath at the Nightless City, three years of brutal confinement had awaited him. Yet midway through that sentence, news had shattered the realm: the heavens were just, evil had met its end, and the Yiling Laozu was dead, his soul torn to shreds.

Dragging a broken body that had barely begun to mend, he had dragged himself to Yiling. He tore through that cursed mountain for days on end, finding nothing among the charred ash except a feverish, half-dead Wen Yuan wedged inside a hollow tree trunk. Not a bone, not a shred of flesh, not even a lingering wisp of a soul remained.

On the long trek back to Gusu, Lan Wangji had bought a jar of Emperor's Smile in Caiyi Town.

The liquor was sweet and fragrant, not the throat-burning rotgut he’d expected. Yet the second it went down, it burned like liquid fire, scorching straight from his throat into his chest and burning behind his eyes.

He hated the taste. But for the first time, he understood why that person had loved it so much.

That night was the first time in Lan Wangji’s life he had ever touched alcohol, and the first time he had ever gotten plastered. Whatever happened during that drunken blackout was entirely lost to him, but for months afterward, every disciple and elder in the Cloud Recesses looked at him with sheer, horrified disbelief. They said he had broken into the ancestral archives, tearing through trunks and shelves in a manic frenzy. When Lan Xichen tried to intervene, Lan Wangji had stared through him with vacant, glassy eyes, demanding a flute.

Lan Xichen had fetched the finest white jade flute in their collection, but Lan Wangji had hurled it away in fury, screaming that it wasn't the right one. Unable to find what he sought, his gaze had landed on the locked vaults holding the confiscated Wen Clan branding irons.

When he finally sobered up, a blistering scar sat seared over his heart—an identical match to the burn Wei Wuxian had carried out of the Xuanwu cave.

Lan Qiren had looked thoroughly heartbroken, yet the fury in his eyes had slowly faded into defeat. Over those three years, the beatings, the lectures, and the punishments had already been dealt in excess.

With a heavy sigh, he dropped his objections to keeping Wen Yuan. Lan Wangji had bowed deeply, accepted his punishment for breaking curfew, and knelt silently before the discipline stones for a day and a night.

To drink the wine he drank. To bear the scars he bore.

Thirteen years had passed, and the scar had long since healed over.

Lan Wangji began to pull back and thrust in a steady, deliberate rhythm. Wei Wuxian squeezed his eyes shut, his jaw clenched as he hissed through his teeth, trying to sync his breath to the heavy shifts above him.

Once the initial shock of the invasion faded, Wei Wuxian shifted his hips just a fraction. A jolt of electric, blinding heat shot straight up from his core, racing up his spine and setting his entire nervous system on fire.

Oh. Just like that, he figured out the trick.

Tangling his fingers through Lan Wangji’s sweat-dampened hair, brushing against the silk of his forehead ribbon, a breathless, wicked smile spread across his lips. “...Feels good, doesn't it? Being inside me?”

Lan Wangji wasn't much for pillow talk; he was a man of action through and through, letting his body do the talking,so he clamped his teeth over Wei Wuxian's lower lip, answering the taunt with a bruising, ruthless snap of his hips.

Sweat poured off Wei Wuxian’s skin until he was drenched from head to toe, yet he couldn't keep his mouth shut, gasping through ragged breaths:“Lan Zhan. Lan Zhan, Lan Zhan... I love you so damn much. I’m yours, only yours—ah!Easy!”

Finally reaping the bitter harvest of his own big mouth, Wei Wuxian threw his arms around him, peppering desperate, appeasing kisses along his jaw, completely abandoning his dignity: “Er-gege, have a heart, leave me with half a life! We have the rest of our days ahead of us, we can keep going next time—tie me to the rafters and fuck me like that next time if you want! Just spare this little virgin for today! The mighty Hanguang-jun wins, the Yiling Laozu surrenders completely, defeated! Let’s call a truce until tomorrow!”

A faint blue vein pulsed at Lan Wangji’s temple. Every syllable dragged out of him with agonizing effort: “…If you truly wish… to stop… then shut… your mouth…”

“But I have a mouth, I have to talk!” Wei Wuxian whined desperately. “Lan Zhan, earlier when I said I wanted to sleep with you every single day… can you just pretend you didn't hear that?!”

Lan Wangji didn't miss a beat. “No.”

Wei Wuxian looked heartbroken. “How can you be so cruel? You’ve never said no to me before!”

A tiny, breathtaking curve touched the corner of Lan Wangji’s lips. “No.”

Seeing that rare, stunning smile, Wei Wuxian’s eyes instantly lit up, a wave of dizzying euphoria washing through him until he barely knew up from down.

The very next second, however, a brutal, relentless snap of Lan Wangji’s hips completely shattered that sweet illusion, driving hot tears straight from the corners of his eyes.

Clawing at the damp earth with both hands, Wei Wuxian wailed at the top of his lungs: “Then every four days! Can we do once every four days?! If four is too much, what about three?!”

Lan Wangji’s reply came down like iron, heavy and indisputable:

“Every day means every day.”
